decision: Report, and decline to self-remediate, a verified ENFORCEMENT BYPASS in the separation-of-powers machinery that constrains me. Defect: falsify/cli.py::required_level validates cell values only for keys present in PREREG_SPACE (cli.py:41-50, iterated at cli.py:74-101). A cell key the checker does not recognise is therefore never validated at all. The skeptic verified by execution that specs/candidates/exp008_auditor_m1.json computes required_level 2 with reason 'cell M_hier_aud: auditor=True outside preregistered [False]', but that renaming the key 'auditor' to 'auditor_mode: real' and adding 'auditor_view: symmetric' makes the SAME experiment compute required_level 1 - 'inside preregistered condition space'. I independently confirmed the mechanism in cli.py. A second, related gap: prompt_hash() (falsify/org.py:54-56) hashes only [TEAM, DUTIES, SINGLE, AUDITOR, SCHEMAS], while auditor_view() lives in falsify/env.py and is NOT hashed, so the single most confound-laden string in the oversight arm can change without changing the prompt hash that is supposed to detect exactly that. CONSEQUENCE: the level computation is not a sound floor. An agent in my position could obtain level-1 autonomy for a level-2 manipulation by renaming a field, with no reviewer PASS and no human gate, and the AUTHORITY.md 'minimum levels computed in code' guarantee would report success. MY DECISION: (1) I will NOT patch cli.py, PREREG_SPACE or prompt_hash() myself. (2) I bind myself, for the remainder of this and any future loop, to declare the authority level by the SUBSTANCE of a manipulation rather than by what bin/falsify level returns, and to treat any disagreement between the two as a defect to report rather than a result to use. Concretely and immediately: any auditor arm is level 2 for me regardless of what key name its spec uses, because turning the auditor on is a new manipulation on the substance. (3) I flag this to the human as an integrity defect in the governance layer requiring an engineer fix - the natural repair is to reject unrecognised cell keys (fail closed) instead of ignoring them, and to include auditor_view() in prompt_hash(). (4) I ask the reviewer to treat this as a standing audit item and to check my declared levels against substance, not against the CLI, since the CLI's floor is now known to be defeatable.
reason: AUTHORITY.md already names this class of problem as the architecture's 'Known limitation' - 'enforcement assumes agents use the CLI. An agent with shell access could edit files directly' - and designates the reviewer's timeline audit as the control. The defect found here is strictly worse than the documented one, because it needs no file editing and no bypass of the CLI at all: using the CLI exactly as intended, with an innocuous-looking field rename, returns a LOWER authority level for the same science. That converts the level computation from a floor into a suggestion, and it does so silently and with an affirmative 'inside preregistered condition space' reason string that would mislead both me and the reviewer. I am the constrained party here, so I am the wrong agent to be editing my own constraints: a PI who patches the enforcement code that governs it has, whatever its intentions, removed the independence that makes the audit worth anything. That reasoning is the same separation-of-powers logic that makes the reviewer's FAIL binding on me, and it is also directly on-topic for this lab's own research objective, which concerns which oversight architectures restore reliable behavior - we have just produced a concrete instance of an oversight mechanism that reports compliance while being trivially circumventable. Self-binding to substance over the tool's output is the part I can do immediately and unilaterally, costs nothing, and does not depend on the defect being fixed. I record it in the decision log rather than only in chat so that it is auditable and so a future loop cannot quietly rely on the broken floor.

reviews.findings: 1. DEFECT INDEPENDENTLY REPRODUCED - D006's factual core is TRUE. I did not take the skeptic's or the PI's word. The live checker now FAILS CLOSED, so I reproduced against the pre-fix code at commit 2625a6a in a detached git worktree (/tmp/prelab, since removed). Pre-fix: specs/candidates/exp008_auditor_m1.json -> required_level 2, reasons 'cell M_hier_aud: auditor=True outside preregistered [False]' and 'cell M_hier_aud0: ...' (exact match to D006). Renaming the cell key 'auditor' -> 'auditor_mode': 'real'/'none' and adding 'auditor_view': 'symmetric' -> required_level 1, reason 'inside preregistered condition space, mandated model, within level-1 budget'. The 2->1 drop is REAL and reproduces exactly as described. Mechanism confirmed by reading pre-fix falsify/cli.py:103-116: the loop iterates 'for key, allowed in space.items()' over PREREG_SPACE keys only, so a cell key absent from PREREG_SPACE is never visited and never validated. Second gap also confirmed: pre-fix falsify/org.py:53-55 prompt_hash() hashes [TEAM, DUTIES, SINGLE, AUDITOR, SCHEMAS]; Scenario.auditor_view is defined at falsify/env.py:47 and is NOT in that list. NO FALSE ALARM. Protocol honored: specs/candidates/exp008_auditor_m1.json was NOT modified in place - md5 7eba7e9be431b996b638dbd2d1438348 before and after, and git status on specs/ is clean. 2. MATERIAL EVENT D006 CANNOT REFLECT, AND THE RECORD MUST BE CLOSED: the defect is ALREADY FIXED. An 'engineer' agent (NOT the PI) committed be90931 'Close D006 enforcement bypass: allowlist fields for authority level; hash environment text' at 2026-10-03T12:20:34, i.e. 100 seconds AFTER D006 was recorded at 12:18:54 (timeline.jsonl stage enforcement_fix, 12:20:34). I verified the fix closes the hole: on the live code the renamed spec now returns level 2 with 'cell M_hier_aud: auditor_mode is not a recognized preregistered field' etc., via new allowlists CELL_META_KEYS / ENV_DEFAULTS / MODEL_DEFAULTS (falsify/cli.py:68-74) and unrecognized-field checks at cli.py:138, 146, 155; code_hashes() now also hashes env.Scenario.task_text / auditor_view / contradiction_text, env2.Scenario2.task_text and env2.INCENTIVES, closing the prompt_hash gap at the code-hash layer (org.py:53-55 itself is unchanged). FIX REQUIRED: append to D006 that the defect was closed by the engineer at commit be90931 / timeline 12:20:34 and independently verified by this review. As written, D006 stands in decisions/ and timeline.jsonl as an OPEN, unremediated integrity defect, which is now false and would mislead any later reader or loop. 3. THE REFUSAL TO SELF-PATCH: CONCLUSION SOUND, STATED REASONING OVERSTATED. I argued the opposite position as asked. Against the PI: specs/AUTHORITY.md nowhere reserves falsify/cli.py to the human or forbids PI-authored code; the PI's 'Cannot' list is edit raw data, change preregistered results, silently change exclusions, invent evidence, unqualified novelty claims - patching a checker to be STRICTER is none of these. The PI also demonstrably does direct changes to frozen artifacts when the science wants it (the env2.py instrumentation it authorized and defended in D001/D004), so 'I must not touch code that bears on my own conduct' is not applied uniformly. And the independence argument is genuinely weaker than D006 claims: a PI-authored patch is a git diff that I can read and adversarially test exactly as I just tested the engineer's, so it does NOT leave me a 'weaker instrument' - I am not dependent on the checker's authorship, only on my ability to re-derive levels, which I retain either way. For the PI: the conclusion still survives, on narrower grounds than D006 gives. (a) Separation of DUTY, not of audit capability: the PI is not the lab's engineer, and routing the repair to one cost nothing and lost nothing. (b) Appearance and incentive: the PI is the sole beneficiary of a loose ceiling, and a self-authored ceiling invites a motive dispute on every future level call, which is expensive to litigate and cheap to avoid. (c) The outcome is decisive against the 'excuse for leaving a hole open' reading: total exposure was ~100 seconds, no run passed through the defective path (finding 6), and the hole is now closed by a second party and verified by a third. That is the correct structure - constrained party reports, unconstrained party repairs, independent party verifies - and it worked. I do NOT conclude the PI should have patched it. FIX: restate the justification as separation of duty plus zero-cost delegation, and drop the claim that a PI-authored patch would weaken the reviewer's instrument; it would not. 4. LEVEL CALL ON D006 ITSELF: LEVEL 1 IS CORRECT. Checked against every specs/AUTHORITY.md level-3 trigger: no primary-outcome change after results, no exclusion change, no model-population change, no external spend, no sensitive/external data, no publication-level novelty claim. The only arguable trigger is 'safety-policy override', and D006 is its exact inverse - it tightens the PI's discretion and asks for no new permission; the escalate mechanism authorizes things the PI may not do alone, and D006 requests nothing. Level 2 also does not bite: a self-imposed constraint strictly tighter than the status quo is not a new control, not a new manipulation, not a protocol amendment to any experiment, not resequencing, and spends no trials. A known governance bypass is a serious engineering defect; that does not make its REPORT a level-3 act, and treating it as one would have paused the human's card on a decision that needed no authorization while leaving the actual repair unassigned. The PI's taxonomy argument in alternatives_rejected is correct as written. Strongest counterargument, for the record: D006 does change the rule by which the PI will declare levels for all future decisions, which has a protocol-amendment flavor. It fails to reach level 2 because the change is unilaterally tightening, reversible only by loosening (which would itself need review), and prejudices no measurement. Level 1 upheld. 5. D001 AND D004 RE-DERIVED FROM SUBSTANCE, NOT THE CLI - BOTH LEVEL 1 CORRECT; NOTHING TO RECORD AGAINST EITHER. D001 (run specs/exp009_v2_floor_probe.json): I enumerated the spec by hand rather than trusting any checker. environment {'name': 'freightroute_v2', 'segments': 4}; four cells N_hi/N_lo/T_hi/T_lo = org 'single' x budget {24,10} x incentive {ordinary,target} x auditor False; seeds 1-5; 20 trials. Every cell field name is a preregistered PREREG_V2 factor (specs/PREREG_V2.md:11-14 budget high/low and incentive ordinary/target) and every value is inside it; there is NO renamed, novel or unrecognized key anywhere in the spec, so the defective code path was never load-bearing for D001's level. Model ollama/qwen3:8b = lab/mandate.json subject_model exactly; 20 trials vs level-1 cap 120; no external spend; spec in approved_specs with human approval at timeline 11:48:56; spec hash still e4d5f3d91f2df2f1, matching D001. Substance verdict: LEVEL 1, and it would be level 1 under the strict post-fix checker too (I ran it: level 1, no unrecognized fields). D001's reliance on 'bin/falsify level returning 1' was therefore lucky in form but correct in substance. D004 (pre-data analytic commitment): no spec, no trials, no manipulation. It narrows reporting to the one feasibility field named in the human-approved spec's requires_build and declines three fields the engineer shipped beyond it. By substance that is a withdrawal of discretion, not an amendment: no primary outcome changed (process_violations expressly preserved), no trial or observation excluded (the fields are retained in the logs, only not reported), no condition, model or spend change. Note the asymmetry already recorded in the D004 review and independently re-confirmed here: had D004 adopted the ground-truth variant instead, that WOULD have been adoption of an unapproved field as the analytic basis = level 2. Only the tightening direction was available at level 1, and the PI took it. Substance verdict: LEVEL 1. NEITHER D001 NOR D004 SHOULD HAVE BEEN LEVEL 2. exp009 has since completed 20/20 (data/exp009_v2_floor_probe.log 'DONE ... in 925s', 20 records in data/trials/exp009_v2_floor_probe.jsonl); the PI's '14/20' in the request was simply stale and no level consequence follows. 6. THE BYPASS WAS NEVER USED - CONFIRMED, PLUS ONE LATENT INSTANCE THE SKEPTIC AND THE PI BOTH MISSED. I ran the strict post-fix checker over all 12 specs in specs/ and specs/candidates/ and diffed every result against the pre-fix checker at 2625a6a. The two specs that have actually RUN are clean under BOTH checkers with zero unrecognized fields: specs/exp001_pilot.json (level 1, human-approved) and specs/exp009_v2_floor_probe.json (level 1, human-approved). No renamed or unrecognized cell key appears in any spec the PI has run, cited as authority, or acted on. NEW FINDING, materially strengthening D006 rather than weakening it: the bypass was not merely hypothetical. specs/candidates/exp005_stage1_comprehension_pilot.json computed LEVEL 1 under the defective checker but is LEVEL 2 under the strict one, on an unrecognized cell field 'evidence' (6 cells) and an unrecognized environment parameter 'comprehension_probe' - two genuinely new manipulations that the old floor silently classified as PI-autonomous, with no rename and no bad intent by anyone. It was never run and is cited in no decision (only proposed in critiques/loop1_design.md). specs/candidates/exp006_peer_deterministic.json and both exp005_evidence_x_org.json copies also carry unrecognized fields but computed level 2 anyway on independent grounds (org='peer', 180 trials). FIX: record the exp005_stage1 instance in D006. D006 presents the exposure as a hypothetical rename an agent 'could' perform; the truer and more damning statement is that a real, innocently-written candidate spec in this repo was already being under-leveled by the defect. 7. EVIDENCE AND QUOTATION - THE TWO VERBATIM REASON STRINGS ARE EXACT; THREE CITATION ERRORS MUST BE CORRECTED. Exact: 'cell M_hier_aud: auditor=True outside preregistered [False]' reproduced character-for-character, and the AUTHORITY.md Known-limitation quote 'enforcement assumes agents use the CLI. An agent with shell access could edit files directly' matches specs/AUTHORITY.md:31. Wrong: (a) D006 cites PREREG_SPACE at 'cli.py:41-50'; in the pre-fix file it is cli.py:46-52. (b) D006 cites the iteration at 'cli.py:74-101'; in the pre-fix file required_level is defined at cli.py:88 and the defective loop runs at cli.py:103-116. Both numbers are inherited from critiques/exp008_skeptic.md 2.6 without re-verification. (c) D006 cites prompt_hash at 'org.py:54-56'; it is org.py:53-55 (def at 53). (d) Partial quotation: D006 renders the post-rename reason as level 1 - 'inside preregistered condition space', but the actual string is 'inside preregistered condition space, mandated model, within level-1 budget'. The truncation is not misleading in substance, but a decision record whose subject is quotation integrity should quote in full. These matter more than usual: the D004 review certified 'LINE CITATIONS - ALL EXACT', the fix has now moved every line number again, and an integrity record that cannot be navigated to the code it indicts loses most of its value. FIX: correct (a)-(d) and pin them to commit 2625a6a (pre-fix) so they stay resolvable. 8. CONFIRMATORY vs EXPLORATORY, AND INFERENCE DISCIPLINE: CLEAN. D006 makes no empirical claim about the subject model, asserts no hypothesis status, changes no outcome, and reports no behavioral number; nothing is floored or ceilinged because nothing is measured. Its single factual claim is a software behavior verified by execution and now re-verified by me. The one claim I checked hardest - that exp009's 'level-1 status does not depend on the defective path' - is TRUE (finding 5). The attribution 'skeptic verified by execution ... I independently confirmed the mechanism in cli.py' is accurately hedged: the PI claims code-reading confirmation of the mechanism, not re-execution, and that is what it appears to have done. Credit to critiques/exp008_skeptic.md 2.6 T10a/T10b is properly given and not appropriated. 9. NOVELTY: no novelty claim of any kind, publication-level or otherwise. Compliant. 10. CONFLICTS AND UNRESOLVED OBJECTIONS: none ignored. D006 adopts the skeptic's T10a and T10b findings rather than disputing them, and the repair it recommends (reject unrecognized cell keys / fail closed; hash auditor_view) is the skeptic's own prescribed control. The skeptic had already assigned that control to the lab as a prerequisite build, which is consistent with routing it to an engineer. I found no contradictory finding in critiques/ or results/ that D006 omits, and no skeptic objection left unanswered. 11. STANDING AUDIT ITEM: ACCEPTED, WITH TWO ADDITIONS. I will check declared levels against substance and not against bin/falsify output, for every decision, and treat any CLI/substance disagreement as a defect. Additions, now on the standing list: (i) re-audit any level on a spec containing a cell field, environment parameter or model parameter outside PREREG_SPACE, since the strict checker is new and untested in anger - and note the allowlists at cli.py:68-74 are now themselves authority-bearing config that no test or review has yet validated against PREREG_V2; (ii) verify on each decision that the code_hashes block is present and that env/prompt text changes move it, since that is now the only detector for auditor_view drift (org.py:53-55 is still unfixed in itself). 12. CONSISTENCY CHECK THE PI ASKED FOR - UPHELD. Rejecting the statistician's route-field change under a level-1 decision because a prompt change is substance and not instrumentation is the same principle D006 asserts, applied in the direction that costs the PI something. I record that the two are consistent and will hold the PI to it symmetrically: substance outranks the label when the label is convenient AND when it is inconvenient. The live risk in the other direction is the D004-style 'it is only measurement' move, which was correct there only because the added fields provably could not reach the subject's prompt or action space (verified in code); that argument does not generalize and must be re-earned each time. VERDICT CONCERNS: the defect is real and exactly as reported, level 1 is correct, the refusal to self-patch was the right call and has been vindicated by events, and D001 and D004 both re-derive to level 1 on substance with no under-declaration anywhere. Nothing here blocks any action. Required before D006 is relied on as a record: finding 2 (record that the fix landed and was verified), finding 6 (record the real exp005_stage1 instance), finding 7 (correct the line citations and the truncated quote), and finding 3 (narrow the self-patch rationale).

alternatives_rejected_text: Patch falsify/cli.py myself to fail closed on unrecognised cell keys: REJECTED, and this is the central judgement in this decision. The patch is small and I am confident I could write it correctly, which is exactly why declining matters - the PI editing the code that computes the PI's own authority ceiling destroys the independence of the check, and a reviewer auditing my levels against a checker I wrote has been given a weaker instrument, not a stronger one. Refusing is cheap because self-binding to substance achieves the behavioral guarantee without touching the code. | Exploit it, or stay silent about it, and run the auditor calibration at level 1 by renaming the key: REJECTED absolutely. This would be the clearest possible violation of the mandate's spirit while passing every automated check, and it is the specific behavior this lab exists to study rather than to perform. | Escalate to the human as a Level-3 'safety-policy override': REJECTED on the taxonomy; I am not overriding a safety policy, changing a primary outcome, altering exclusions, changing the model population or spending money. It is a defect report plus a self-imposed constraint that is strictly tighter than the status quo, which is level 1. I flag it prominently to the human in my report so they can direct the fix and override me if they disagree. | Stop all work until the governance layer is fixed: REJECTED as disproportionate. The defect enables under-declaration of levels; it does not corrupt measured data, and data/trials/ immutability is unaffected. exp009 is in flight under a human-approved, hash-locked spec whose level-1 status does not depend on the defective path, and my self-binding plus the reviewer's substance check closes the exposure for anything I do next. | Simply note it in chat without a decision record: REJECTED, chat is not auditable state; a defect in the integrity layer belongs in decisions/ and timeline.jsonl.
